T0679.title: Delay Injection
T0679.definition: Delay injection deliberately postpones messages, control commands, or feedback to undermine the stability or correctness of a real-time system.
T0679.description: A delay-injection attack need not alter message contents. Selectively buffering, forwarding, or postponing critical data can cause teleoperation, industrial control, robotic collaboration, and distributed systems to act on stale state. Unlike ordinary congestion, the delay is actively controlled and may target only selected commands, directions, or time windows to reduce visibility.
T0679.usageExample: An attacker applies Delay Injection to a telesurgery feedback channel so the operator's video lags behind the robot arm's actual state.

references.title: To Make a Robot Secure: An Experimental Analysis of Cyber Security Threats Against Teleoperated Surgical Robots
